Consult Summary:
- 19-year-old female presents with a 3-day history of stinging dysuria and mild lower abdominal cramping during urination, with one episode of minor hematuria and malodorous urine; afebrile, no flank pain or systemic symptoms. Clinical impression: uncomplicated lower UTI; empiric 3-day antibiotic course prescribed, hydration advised, red flags and follow-up discussed.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Pain/stinging with urination for a few days; mild lower abdominal “crampy” pain associated with urination.
- Associated symptoms: One episode of a small amount of blood in urine today; urine odor noted as unusual.
- Negatives: No urinary frequency increase reported; no back/flank pain; no nausea/vomiting; no fever; no vaginal discharge.
- Bowel: Normal; no diarrhea.
- Gynecologic: Last menstrual period “a couple of weeks ago” (doctor repeated “three weeks ago”—see conflict). Patient does not believe she is pregnant.
- Sexual history: Sexually active with a boyfriend of a couple of months; uses condoms; has never had an STI screen.

Past Medical History:
- Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS). No other chronic conditions reported.

Medications:
- Regular medications: None reported.
- Recent/OTC: Over-the-counter bicarbonate taken a few days ago for urinary symptoms; not helpful (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: Clindamycin — causes swelling (suggesting significant hypersensitivity).

Social History:
- Lives in a flat near college with friends.
- Student (studying biology).
- Tobacco: Does not smoke.
- Alcohol: Drinks socially on weekends.
- Contraception: Condoms.

Family History:
- Denies known family history of kidney, bladder, or gastrointestinal diseases.

Physical Examination:
- Not documented.

Investigations:
- None obtained/documented (no urinalysis, urine culture, pregnancy test, or STI screening documented).

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Dysuria with minor hematuria and suprapubic cramping — likely uncomplicated lower UTI (cystitis).
  - Antibiotic: Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim prescribed; “1 tablet twice daily for 3 days.” Specific agent and dose/strength not documented; route not documented.
  - Supportive care: Increase oral fluids; cranberry juice may help symptoms.
  - Sexual activity: Advise avoiding intercourse until symptoms resolve; continue barrier contraception thereafter.
  - Safety net: Seek care if fever, back/flank pain, or systemic worsening occurs (concern for ascending infection/pyelonephritis).
  - Follow-up: If not improved by end of the week, call or return for reassessment.
  - Pregnancy: If any concern about pregnancy, perform a pregnancy test (patient does not think she is pregnant).
- Issue 2: Sexual health screening.
  - Context: New partner; uses condoms; never had STI screen; no vaginal discharge reported.
  - Plan: No STI testing ordered/documented today.
- Issue 3: Medication allergy.
  - Clindamycin allergy (swelling) — avoid clindamycin and document prominently.

General Plan items:
- None beyond above.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals; physical exam findings; urinalysis and/or urine culture; pregnancy test; STI screening; exact antibiotic selection and dose/strength; medication reconciliation beyond current report; immunization history; past surgical history.
- Internal conflicts: LMP timing—patient stated “a couple of weeks ago,” doctor restated “three weeks ago” (conflict noted). Brief initial uncertainty about fever due to audio; ultimately patient confirmed no fever.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor audio dropouts and filler words, but key clinical details captured.
